title: Who, which, that
theme: Relative clauses defining (who, which, that, where, whose)
goal: Student describes people, things, and places using defining relative clauses.

units.title: The person who
units.grammar_focus: who for people in defining clauses
units.real_life_context: You describe people by what they do.

grammar.sentence: She's the woman _____ lives next door.
grammar.explanation: "Who" for people in defining relative clauses.

grammar.sentence: He's the man _____ called yesterday.
The doctor _____ helps me is kind.
I know a girl _____ speaks five languages.
She's the friend _____ I told you about.
The teacher _____ teaches us is great.
He's the guy _____ won the race.
He's the man which called me.
grammar.hint: which is for things, not people
grammar.answer: He's the man who called me.

grammar.sentence: "She's the girl, who lives here." (defining = no comma)
grammar.answer: She's the girl who lives here.
grammar.explanation: Defining clauses have NO commas. Identifies which girl.

grammar.passage: She's the woman who works with me. He's the man who called yesterday. They're the people who live next door.
grammar.question: Who works with the speaker?
grammar.explanation: The text says "the woman who works with me".

listening_speaking.text: She's the woman who lives next door.
He's the man who called.
The doctor who helps me is kind.
I know a girl who speaks five languages.
She's the friend I told you about.

units.title: The book which
units.grammar_focus: which/that for things in defining clauses

grammar.sentence: It's a book _____ changed my life.
grammar.explanation: "Which" for things in defining clauses. "That" also works.

grammar.sentence: I have a phone _____ works underwater.
She bought a car _____ runs on electricity.
This is the movie _____ won the Oscar.
I love books _____ teach me something.
The phone _____ I bought is broken.
grammar.explanation: "The phone that I bought" — object: that/which/omitted.

grammar.sentence: It's the song _____ I love.
The book who I read was great.
grammar.answer: The book that I read was great.

grammar.sentence: "He has a car, which is red." (defining = no comma)
grammar.answer: He has a car which is red.
grammar.explanation: Defining → no comma. Non-defining (info adicional) → comma — but M19 covers that.

grammar.passage: I have a phone which has a great camera. I love books that take me to other worlds.
grammar.question: What does the speaker love about books?
grammar.explanation: The text says "books that take me to other worlds".

listening_speaking.text: It's a book which changed my life.
I have a phone that works underwater.
She bought a car which runs on electricity.
This is the movie that won the Oscar.
I love books that teach me something.

units.title: Whose
units.real_life_context: You describe people by what they own or who's related.

grammar.sentence: She's the woman _____ husband is a doctor.
He's the guy _____ car broke down.
I know a man _____ daughter is famous.
She's the friend _____ birthday is today.
He's the teacher _____ class I love.
It's the dog _____ name I forgot.
She's the woman _____ kids are in my class.
He's the man who's car is red.
grammar.answer: He's the man whose car is red.

grammar.sentence: She's the friend her name is Ana.
grammar.hint: Use whose for possession in relative clause

grammar.passage: She's the woman whose husband is a doctor. He's the guy whose car I borrowed. I have a friend whose birthday is today.
